items.stem: A user can change the id in a URL to view another user's record. Which flaw is this?

options.text: Broken access control (insecure direct object reference)
options.rationale: Correct: this is an IDOR, a form of broken access control.
No database query is being manipulated here.
No script is being injected into a page.
Viewing another record does not deny service.

items.explanation: Correct: changing an id to reach another's record is an IDOR / broken access control.

items.stem: Which TWO must be confirmed before testing a web application? (Select TWO.)

options.text: An agreed scope of what may be tested
options.rationale: Correct: a defined scope prevents out-of-bounds testing.
Tester preference does not define legality or scope.

options.text: A promise that no bugs will be found
options.rationale: No such promise is possible or relevant.

items.explanation: Correct: written authorisation and an agreed scope must both be confirmed first.

items.stem: Why is client-side input validation insufficient on its own to prevent SQL injection?

options.text: An attacker can bypass the client and send crafted requests directly to the server
options.rationale: Correct: server-side validation is required because clients can be bypassed.

options.text: SQL injection only affects the browser
options.rationale: SQL injection targets the server-side database.
Servers do receive and must validate input.

items.explanation: Correct: clients can be bypassed, so server-side validation is essential.
